data.narrative: The student chose API keys for the internal admin surface, mapped two keys to principal_id, kept GET /r/{code} public, and proved 401/200/404/307/429 over ASGI. BREAK injected a real IDOR on GET /api/admin/links (B listed A's URL); FIX restored the owner filter and moved keys into env so JWT_SECRET is no longer an API-key alias. Create/redirect proofs used the in-process store because localhost:5432 is down — that limit was recorded, not faked.

dimension_scores.observation: Picked API keys over JWT because revoke-by-rotation fits an internal admin API, and 404 over 403 to hide link existence.
dimension_scores.evidence: DECIDE A recorded; not_owner_status=404; GET_A_AS_B_STATUS 404 with body Link not found and no long_url leak.

dimension_scores.observation: Injected an IDOR, reproduced the leak with a two-principal ASGI script, then closed it with the same script as a regression.
dimension_scores.evidence: BREAK_IDOR_LEAK True with B listing https://secret.example/a-private; after FIX, FIX_IDOR_LEAK False and FIX_LIST_B_BODY count 0 items [].

dimension_scores.observation: Separated authN from authZ, rate-limited create/redirect/analytics, and stopped treating JWT_SECRET as a second principal-a key.
dimension_scores.evidence: CREATE_RATE 200x5 then 429; REDIRECT 307x8 then 429; ANALYTICS 200x5 then 429; FIX_JWT_SECRET_AS_API_KEY_STATUS 401; config rejects shared/short keys.

dimension_scores.observation: Did not claim Postgres 2xx while the database is down; used an in-process owner-scoped store and named that remaining risk.
dimension_scores.evidence: CREATE_A_BODY persisted=memory; reflect notes in-memory limiter/store will not survive restart or multi-worker until Redis/Postgres are up.

dimension_scores.observation: Artifacts quote exact status arrays and the IDOR leak/fix bodies instead of paraphrasing.
dimension_scores.evidence: progress/system-design-module4-break.md and fix.md include BREAK_LIST_B_BODY and FIX_LIST_B_BODY; verify script prints RATE_LIMIT_MATRIX.

strengths: Two-principal owner-scope proof: A 200 / B 404 on get, analytics, and delete, with public redirect still 307.
Rate-limit matrix proven with 429 after documented limits, not just declared in comments.
Honest environment bound: no fabricated Postgres insert success.
growth_areas: Persist owner-scoped links in Postgres and share rate limits via Redis once localhost:5432 and :6379 are serving.
data.recommendation: When Postgres is available, add created_by to the links row and make GET /api/admin/links a SELECT ... WHERE created_by = :principal so the owner filter cannot drift between memory and DB.

public_evidence.artifact: API-key auth and owner-scoped link CRUD
public_evidence.student_action: Required X-API-Key on create/get/delete/analytics/admin list and scoped records to principal_id with 404 for non-owners.
public_evidence.technical_detail: api/app/auth.py maps API_KEY_A/API_KEY_B from env to principal-a/principal-b; api/app/main.py POST /links, GET/DELETE /links/{code}, GET /links/{code}/analytics, GET /api/admin/links.
public_evidence.proof: ASGI module04_auth_verify.py: POST /links without key 401; with key A 200; GET A's code as B 404; GET /r/{code} 307 without a key.
public_evidence.ability: Designs public vs protected API surfaces with identity and authorization.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the student can keep a public redirect product while locking writes and reads to an owner.

public_evidence.student_action: Implemented an in-process sliding window and proved 429 after the documented matrix.
public_evidence.proof: CREATE_RATE_STATUSES 200 x5 then 429 x2; REDIRECT_RATE_STATUSES 307 x8 then 429 x2; ANALYTICS_RATE_STATUSES 200 x5 then 429 x2.
public_evidence.ability: Adds abuse controls that can be demonstrated with a tight loop.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Rate limits are specified and measured, not only mentioned in design notes.

public_evidence.student_action: Reproduced a missing owner filter on GET /api/admin/links, restored the filter, and moved API keys into validated env vars.
public_evidence.technical_detail: list_links filters rec.owner == principal_id; config requires distinct API_KEY_A/API_KEY_B of length >=32 and not equal to JWT_SECRET.
public_evidence.proof: module04_auth_break.py before fix leaked A's URL to B; after fix FIX_IDOR_LEAK False and JWT_SECRET as X-API-Key returns 401.
public_evidence.ability: Finds authorization bugs that survive authentication and closes them with a regression check.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Distinguishes 'logged in' from 'allowed to see this row', which is the usual production IDOR class.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: 401 without/wrong key vs 404 when a valid key reads another principal's link.
Admin list returned another owner's original_url until the owner filter was restored.
Removed JWT_SECRET from the API_KEYS map so rotating JWT_SECRET cannot leave a second principal-a credential.

teaching_approaches.detail: Two API keys, create as A, read as B, compare 200 vs 404 bodies.
